chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What is the meaning of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: 'And whoever keeps it alive, it is as though he kept alive all the people'?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'From burning or drowning.' I said, 'So (what about) the one who extracts it from straying to Guidance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is its greatest interpretation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the deeper meaning of 'whoever keeps it alive' in Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:32 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the literal preservation of physical life from death and the superior spiritual act of guiding a believer from error to divine truth, a concept central to Shia hermeneutics. This hadith underscores the theological priority of *hidayah* (guidance) over mere biological survival, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the inner dimension of faith. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the multifaceted nature of 'reviving the soul' in Islamic jurisprudence and spirituality.
